paragraphs.text: For we know that if the earthly house of our tabernacle be dissolved, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal, in the heavens.
paragraphs.original: Οἴδαμεν γὰρ ὅτι ἐὰν ἡ ἐπίγειος ἡμῶν οἰκία τοῦ σκήνους καταλυθῇ, οἰκοδομὴν ἐκ θεοῦ ἔχομεν οἰκίαν ἀχειροποίητον αἰώνιον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: Oidamen gar hoti ean hē epigeios hēmōn oikia tou skēnous katalythē, oikodomēn ek theou echomen oikian acheiropoiēton aiōnion en tois ouranois.

paragraphs.text: For verily in this we groan, longing to be clothed upon with our habitation which is from heaven:
paragraphs.original: καὶ γὰρ ἐν τούτῳ στενάζομεν, τὸ οἰκητήριον ἡμῶν τὸ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐπενδύσασθαι ἐπιποθοῦντες,
paragraphs.translit: kai gar en toutō stenazomen, to oikētērion hēmōn to ex ouranou ependysasthai epipothountes,

paragraphs.text: if so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked.
paragraphs.original: εἴ γε καὶ ἐνδυσάμενοι οὐ γυμνοὶ εὑρεθησόμεθα.
paragraphs.translit: ei ge kai endysamenoi ou gymnoi heurethēsometha.

paragraphs.text: For indeed we that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened; not for that we would be unclothed, but that we would be clothed upon, that what is mortal may be swallowed up of life.
paragraphs.original: καὶ γὰρ οἱ ὄντες ἐν τῷ σκήνει στενάζομεν βαρούμενοι ἐφʼ ᾧ οὐ θέλομεν ἐκδύσασθαι ἀλλʼ ἐπενδύσασθαι, ἵνα καταποθῇ τὸ θνητὸν ὑπὸ τῆς ζωῆς.
paragraphs.translit: kai gar hoi ontes en tō skēnei stenazomen baroumenoi ephʼ hō ou thelomen ekdysasthai allʼ ependysasthai, hina katapothē to thnēton hypo tēs zōēs.

paragraphs.text: Now he that wrought us for this very thing is God, who gave unto us the earnest of the Spirit.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ κατεργασάμενος ἡμᾶς εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο θεός, ὁ δοὺς ἡμῖν τὸν ἀρραβῶνα τοῦ πνεύματος.
paragraphs.translit: ho de katergasamenos hēmas eis auto touto theos, ho dous hēmin ton arrabōna tou pneumatos.

paragraphs.text: Being therefore always of good courage, and knowing that, whilst we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord
paragraphs.original: Θαρροῦντες οὖν πάντοτε καὶ εἰδότες ὅτι ἐνδημοῦντες ἐν τῷ σώματι ἐκδημοῦμεν ἀπὸ τοῦ κυρίου,
paragraphs.translit: Tharrountes oun pantote kai eidotes hoti endēmountes en tō sōmati ekdēmoumen apo tou kyriou,

paragraphs.text: (for we walk by faith, not by sight);
paragraphs.original: διὰ πίστεως γὰρ περιπατοῦμεν, οὐ διὰ εἴδους—
paragraphs.translit: dia pisteōs gar peripatoumen, ou dia eidous—

paragraphs.text: we are of good courage, I say, and are willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be at home with the Lord.
paragraphs.original: θαρροῦμεν δὲ καὶ εὐδοκοῦμεν μᾶλλον ἐκδημῆσαι ἐκ τοῦ σώματος καὶ ἐνδημῆσαι πρὸς τὸν κύριον·
paragraphs.translit: tharroumen de kai eudokoumen mallon ekdēmēsai ek tou sōmatos kai endēmēsai pros ton kyrion·

paragraphs.text: Wherefore also we make it our aim, whether at home or absent, to be well-pleasing unto him.
paragraphs.original: διὸ καὶ φιλοτιμούμεθα, εἴτε ἐνδημοῦντες εἴτε ἐκδημοῦντες, εὐάρεστοι αὐτῷ εἶναι.
paragraphs.translit: dio kai philotimoumetha, eite endēmountes eite ekdēmountes, euarestoi autō einai.

paragraphs.text: For we must all be made manifest before the judgment-seat of Christ; that each one may receive the things [done] in the body, according to what he hath done, whether [it be] good or bad.
paragraphs.original: τοὺς γὰρ πάντας ἡμᾶς φανερωθῆναι δεῖ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ βήματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἵνα κομίσηται ἕκαστος τὰ διὰ τοῦ σώματος πρὸς ἃ ἔπραξεν, εἴτε ἀγαθὸν εἴτε φαῦλον.
paragraphs.translit: tous gar pantas hēmas phanerōthēnai dei emprosthen tou bēmatos tou Christou, hina komisētai hekastos ta dia tou sōmatos pros ha epraxen, eite agathon eite phaulon.

paragraphs.text: Knowing therefore the fear of the Lord, we persuade men, but we are made manifest unto God; and I hope that we are made manifest also in your consciences.
paragraphs.original: Εἰδότες οὖν τὸν φόβον τοῦ κυρίου ἀνθρώπους πείθομεν, θεῷ δὲ πεφανερώμεθα· ἐλπίζω δὲ καὶ ἐν ταῖς συνειδήσεσιν ὑμῶν πεφανερῶσθαι.
paragraphs.translit: Eidotes oun ton phobon tou kyriou anthrōpous peithomen, theō de pephanerōmetha· elpizō de kai en tais syneidēsesin hymōn pephanerōsthai.

paragraphs.text: We are not again commending ourselves unto you, but [speak] as giving you occasion of glorying on our behalf, that ye may have wherewith to answer them that glory in appearance, and not in heart.
paragraphs.original: οὐ πάλιν ἑαυτοὺς συνιστάνομεν ὑμῖν, ἀλλὰ ἀφορμὴν διδόντες ὑμῖν καυχήματος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, ἵνα ἔχητε πρὸς τοὺς ἐν προσώπῳ καυχωμένους καὶ μὴ ἐν καρδίᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: ou palin heautous synistanomen hymin, alla aphormēn didontes hymin kauchēmatos hyper hēmōn, hina echēte pros tous en prosōpō kauchōmenous kai mē en kardia.

paragraphs.text: For whether we are beside ourselves, it is unto God; or whether we are of sober mind, it is unto you.
paragraphs.original: εἴτε γὰρ ἐξέστημεν, θεῷ· εἴτε σωφρονοῦμεν, ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: eite gar exestēmen, theō· eite sōphronoumen, hymin.

paragraphs.text: For the love of Christ constraineth us; because we thus judge, that one died for all, therefore all died;
paragraphs.original: ἡ γὰρ ἀγάπη τοῦ Χριστοῦ συνέχει ἡμᾶς, κρίναντας τοῦτο ὅτι εἷς ὑπὲρ πάντων ἀπέθανεν· ἄρα οἱ πάντες ἀπέθανον·
paragraphs.translit: hē gar agapē tou Christou synechei hēmas, krinantas touto hoti heis hyper pantōn apethanen· ara hoi pantes apethanon·

paragraphs.text: and he died for all, that they that live should no longer live unto themselves, but unto him who for their sakes died and rose again.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὑπὲρ πάντων ἀπέθανεν ἵνα οἱ ζῶντες μηκέτι ἑαυτοῖς ζῶσιν ἀλλὰ τῷ ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ἀποθανόντι καὶ ἐγερθέντι.
paragraphs.translit: kai hyper pantōn apethanen hina hoi zōntes mēketi heautois zōsin alla tō hyper autōn apothanonti kai egerthenti.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore we henceforth know no man after the flesh: even though we have known Christ after the flesh, yet now we know [him so] no more.
paragraphs.original: Ὥστε ἡμεῖς ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν οὐδένα οἴδαμεν κατὰ σάρκα· εἰ καὶ ἐγνώκαμεν κατὰ σάρκα Χριστόν, ἀλλὰ νῦν οὐκέτι γινώσκομεν.
paragraphs.translit: Hōste hēmeis apo tou nyn oudena oidamen kata sarka· ei kai egnōkamen kata sarka Christon, alla nyn ouketi ginōskomen.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore if any man is in Christ, [he is] a new creature: the old things are passed away; behold, they are become new.
paragraphs.original: ὥστε εἴ τις ἐν Χριστῷ, καινὴ κτίσις· τὰ ἀρχαῖα παρῆλθεν, ἰδοὺ γέγονεν καινά·
paragraphs.translit: hōste ei tis en Christō, kainē ktisis· ta archaia parēlthen, idou gegonen kaina·

paragraphs.text: But all things are of God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ, and gave unto us the ministry of reconciliation;
paragraphs.original: τὰ δὲ πάντα ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ καταλλάξαντος ἡμᾶς ἑαυτῷ διὰ Χριστοῦ καὶ δόντος ἡμῖν τὴν διακονίαν τῆς καταλλαγῆς,
paragraphs.translit: ta de panta ek tou theou tou katallaxantos hēmas heautō dia Christou kai dontos hēmin tēn diakonian tēs katallagēs,

paragraphs.text: to wit, that God was in Christ reconciling the world unto himself, not reckoning unto them their trespasses, and having committed unto us the word of reconciliation.
paragraphs.original: ὡς ὅτι θεὸς ἦν ἐν Χριστῷ κόσμον καταλλάσσων ἑαυτῷ, μὴ λογιζόμενος αὐτοῖς τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν, καὶ θέμενος ἐν ἡμῖν τὸν λόγον τῆς καταλλαγῆς.
paragraphs.translit: hōs hoti theos ēn en Christō kosmon katallassōn heautō, mē logizomenos autois ta paraptōmata autōn, kai themenos en hēmin ton logon tēs katallagēs.

paragraphs.text: We are ambassadors therefore on behalf of Christ, as though God were entreating by us: we beseech [you] on behalf of Christ, be ye reconciled to God.
paragraphs.original: ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ οὖν πρεσβεύομεν ὡς τοῦ θεοῦ παρακαλοῦντος διʼ ἡμῶν· δεόμεθα ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ, καταλλάγητε τῷ θεῷ.
paragraphs.translit: hyper Christou oun presbeuomen hōs tou theou parakalountos diʼ hēmōn· deometha hyper Christou, katallagēte tō theō.

paragraphs.text: Him who knew no sin he made [to be] sin on our behalf; that we might become the righteousness of God in him.
paragraphs.original: τὸν μὴ γνόντα ἁμαρτίαν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἁμαρτίαν ἐποίησεν, ἵνα ἡμεῖς γενώμεθα δικαιοσύνη θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: ton mē gnonta hamartian hyper hēmōn hamartian epoiēsen, hina hēmeis genōmetha dikaiosynē theou en autō.
